unit.why: A single narrative, quoted from Shvil Emunah, about R. Yosef of Yampol's soul-ascent during illness and judgment in heaven, interwoven with the death of his father R. Yehiel Michel of Zlotchov, ending with a moral coda.

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ הנ"ל שביל אמונה שביל ג'.
stories.end_quote: לתמים במעשיו וטוב לו בזה עכ"ל
stories.summary_en: While gravely ill, R. Yosef of Yampol ascends to the heavenly court, where an angel blows away all his prayers. At that hour his father, the Maggid of Zlotchov, dies in ecstatic devekut at the third Sabbath meal. The Besht intercedes in heaven and has Yosef pray the morning prayer there, which restores all his prayers. Yosef revives, recovers and tells his mother and sister that their father has died; a moral lesson on sincere worship follows.
